newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh to get $370 mln food aid in next 4 yrs.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh to get $370 mln food aid in next 4 yrs.

text.p: Bangladesh, grappling with massive hunger and malnutrition, will receive food aid worth $370 million over the next four years from international donors, World Food Programme (WFP) said.
Of the amount, $162 million would come from the WFP and the rest from bilateral donors, a WFP press release said on Tuesday.
The fund will create seasonal employment opportunities to some 900,000 poor Bangladeshi men and women under two separate food assisted programmes.
The WFP says Bangladesh has the largest food-assisted development programme in the world.
Besides the WFP, Canada, Australia, France and European Union are among the major food aid donors to Bangladesh.
With a population of nearly 120 million people, Bangladesh suffers from food shortage and malnutrition although it produces about 20 million tons of grains a year.
The shortfall is met by international aid and imports.
Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina said on Tuesday that 86 percent of the country's population did not have two nutritious meals a day.
